title: Embedspace smokewalk: multilingual probe and clustering playbook
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a lightweight, high-signal probe (a.k.a. 'smokewalk') for new embedding models being onboarded to Redwood. The goal is to rapidly detect common cross-lingual and clustering regressions that harm semantic search and downstream retrieval features.

Scope and constraints:
- Fast (run in < 2 hours on a dev GPU or CPU cluster)
- Small, interpretable gold set (1.2k–2k items) that covers: short queries, sentence-level docs, longer paragraphs, code-snippets, and metadata-like strings (titles, product names)
- Multi-lingual: EN, ES, FR, DE, ZH, JA, PT, AR, HI (splice in low-resource examples as available)
- Focus metrics: cross-lang translation alignment, within-lang clustering purity, retrieval recall@k, and neighborhood jitter robustness (see metrics section)

Why different from other eval sets:
- Explicitly includes "anchor pairs" (literal translations and paraphrases) plus adversarial near-negatives (lexical overlap but different semantics). This amplifies sensitivity to tokenization and subword mismatches that often trip quantized models.
- Adds micro-slices: code-like tokens, product SKUs, and short titles where embeddings often collapse to degenerate vectors.
- Includes a small synthetic set of machine translations with injected noise (character swaps, punctuation changes) to exercise robustness to noisy inputs typical from user-generated content.

Dataset composition (high level):
- Total items: 1,600 examples
  - Anchors/translations pairs: 400 pairs (800 items) – English + one other language per pair
  - Monolingual cluster groups: 30 clusters × 10 examples = 300 items (English-dominant topical clusters)
  - Micro-slices (short titles, SKUs, code lines): 200 items
  - Negatives and near-neighbors: 150 items (close-token overlap but different meaning)
  - Synthetic noisy translations/perturbations: 150 items

Example anchor pair (English <-> Spanish):
- EN: "How do I reset my API key?"
- ES: "¿Cómo restablezco mi clave de API?"

Example near-negative (should NOT be near in embedding space):
- EN: "Reset API key for integrations"
- EN (near-negative): "Install API key for new hardware"  (shared tokens but different intent)

Micro-slice examples to include:
- Short product titles ("Redwood Inference — 4XL GPU"),
- SKUs ("RDW-23-AX12"),
- Code: "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -d 'text=hello'"

Evaluation metrics (fast, interpretable):
1) Translation alignment mean cosine (per-anchor): mean(cos(embedding(en), embedding(translated))) — expect >= baseline - 0.02 for new models compared to redwood-embed-v1 (baseline)
2) Recall@1/5 on anchor retrieval: Treat translated form as query and expect its English anchor in top-k. Target: recall@1 >= 0.70, recall@5 >= 0.92 (on this small set)
3) Cluster purity (majority-language purity and topical purity): simple kNN label majority; expect purity >= 0.84 for topical clusters
4) Silhouette score for monolingual topical clusters: expect silhouette > 0.12 (small set, conservative)
5) Neighborhood jitter: for 10 random seeds, add small token-level noise (drop punctuation, swap two characters) and compute average rank variance of the true neighbor. Flag if rank variance > threshold (e.g., variance > 50 positions)
6) Token-collapse detector: fraction of items with cosine>0.995 to >5 other points (degeneracy). Should be < 0.5%

Quick failure-mode taxonomy (observed in prior onboarding runs):
- Cross-lingual collapse: translations map to very different regions (cosine < 0.5) — often due to vocab mismatch or aggressive quantization
- Degenerate short-text vectors: titles and SKUs cluster together irrespective of semantics — sign of pooling error or insufficient sentence-level fine-tuning
- Over-clustering by language: model separates by language more than by meaning (good translation alignment metric with low within-lang purity helps detect this)
- Tokenizer misalignment: code snippets tokenized into many subwords and collapse after pooling (look at token counts and avg norm)

Baseline models to run in smokewalk: (names are representative)
- redwood-embed-v1 (gold baseline)
- open-embed-650m-fp16 (reference)
- candidate_model_x (new onboard model under test)

Quick run instructions (dev-friendly):
1) Pull dataset: ./scripts/fetch-embed-smokewalk.sh (local JSONL)
2) Run embeddings for all models with batching 64 (or CPU fallback) and persist vectors with metadata (id, language, cluster_id, slice)
3) Use analysis notebook smokewalk_analysis.ipynb to produce quick metrics and plots (rank histograms, cosine vs length, silhouette)
4) Save report to /shared/reports/embed-smokewalk/{model-name}/{date}/summary.json and attach to jira EMb-4421

Planned experiments / probes to add (tickets):
- CLUST-IF: Add a geodesic interpolation probe: linearly interpolate vectors between translation pairs and check monotonicity of nearest neighbors. (jira:EMB-4490)
- Tokenization sensitivity sweep: compare BPE merges and subword counts vs collapse rate (jira:EMB-4491)
- Quantization stress test: run 4-bit quantized variant and measure translation alignment delta (jira:EMB-4492)

Notes to reviewers / TODOs:
- Add low-resource languages (swahili, urdu) if we can get 30–50 quality anchor pairs (owner: Marco)
- Confirm thresholds with product search team (Riley to sync) — some product teams prefer aggressive recall at cost of precision
- Hook this smokewalk into the CI onboarding job so it runs for every model candidate PR (ops ticket pending)

Quick checklist for pass/fail (suggested):
- Translation mean cosine within 0.02 of baseline OR recall@5 >= baseline - 0.05
- Cluster purity >= 0.80
- Token-collapse < 1%
- No catastrophic degenerate micro-slice collapse (manual spot-check of top-10 nearest neighbors for 10 micro-slice examples)

Appendix: small sample of entries (id | language | text | cluster_id | notes) — include 12 representative rows in the dataset (to be expanded into JSONL)

2 | es | "¿Cómo restablezco mi clave de API?" | anchor_001 | translated

4 | de | "Wie setze ich meinen API-Schlüssel zurück?" | anchor_002 | loosely paraphrased
5 | en | "RDW-23-AX12" | micro_sku_01 | SKU micro-slice
6 | en | "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -d 'text=hello'" | micro_code_01 | code micro-slice
7 | fr | "Comment réinitialiser ma clé API ?" | anchor_001 | translated
8 | en | "Install API key for new hardware" | negative_01 | near-negative intent
9 | zh | "如何重置我的 API 密钥？" | anchor_001 | translated
10 | pt | "Como redefinir minha chave de API?" | anchor_001 | translated

End of smokewalk playbook (working draft)
